# ChatTJB: The chat service powered by AI… ‘Average Individuals’

ChatTJB appears like a regular chatbot, but it is one of a kind. Created by former Google employee Tucker Bryant as an art project, it has attracted more than 100,000 prompts. Answering them are not bots but real people

Advertisement

![Image 20: ChatTJB looks like an AI chatbot, but its answers come from real people, not artificial intelligence, making it a deliberately human alternative to automated chat services. File image/Reuters ](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/08/Untitled-design-35-2026-08-04fe813ccf6f7efcefbae4a175a21620-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

ChatTJB looks like an AI chatbot, but its answers come from real people, not artificial intelligence, making it a deliberately human alternative to automated chat services. File image/Reuters 

[Annapurna.Rai](link_30)|Aug 30, 2026, 17:57:13 IST

We are becoming more and more AI-dependent. From medical advice to relationship tips, we turn to chatbots for everything. Now, Tucker Bryant, a former Google employee, is challenging that. He is the brains behind ChatTJB. It is a chat service, but there is a catch.

Yes, AI is involved, but it is not Artificial Intelligence. ChatTJB is powered by “Average Individuals”. It has real people answering questions.

## **How ChatTJB was born**

ChatTJB looks a lot like other [AI chatbots](link_31). There is a box where users type a question and await a response. However, there is no large language model, algorithm, or automated system spewing an answer. A person reads the question, thinks about it and writes back.

But what pushed the 32-year-old Bryant to create this project in the age of [AI](link_32)? He caught himself asking a chatbot whether to wear short or long sleeves on a day when temperatures were hovering around 18 degrees Celsius in a city where he had lived for seven years. His partner then told him about “cognitive surrender”, the idea that people can hand over part of their thinking to AI rather than making decisions themselves.

![Image 21: explainers](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/explainers.svg)More from Explainers

[ChatGPT Ads in India: What is OpenAI’s new advertising model and what changes for users?](link_33)[How Meta’s $17-billion deal could change Instagram and Facebook for teens](link_34)

![Image 22](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/08/Untitled-design-36-2026-08-a82044a49b9c8ab0edf86378031022e7.jpg)

Former Google employee Tucker Bryant created ChatTJB as an art project to question how dependent people have become on AI. Image courtesy: iamtucks/Instagram

Cognitive surrender is real. It is backed by research from Wharton professors Steven D Shaw and Gideon Nave. Their work found that people using AI assistance could perform better when the AI was correct, but when it gave incorrect advice, their accuracy fell by 15 percentage points compared with people who received no AI assistance.

## **The chat service with no bot**

Bryant launched ChatTJB in April as an art project. However, it caught attention after a billboard advertising the website went up in San Francisco, a hub for AI innovation.

In tune with the “Average Individuals” joke, the website describes the service in technological language, calling it “artisanal intelligence” and a “single-operator large language experience” built on a “human-grounded inference layer”. In reality, its explanation is much simpler: you ask a question, and a human answers when they are “awake and motivated”.

Advertisement

Advertisement

> [](link_35)

Obviously, the waiting time is longer. Instead of a computer processing a request in seconds, users wait for somebody to actually consider what they have written.

The service goes on to say that there is no “mixture of experts”, only a “mixture of moods”, while errors are presented as honest mistakes that can be traced to the human who made them.

At first, Bryant was answering the questions alone. But he was overwhelmed by the inquiries. More than 100,000 prompts were reportedly submitted since the billboard went up. At one point, ChatTJB was receiving more than 5,000 prompts an hour. That was far beyond what Bryant could answer himself.

That is when he turned to volunteers. More than 10,000 people have applied to help, while the volunteer waitlist has been growing by roughly 1,000 people a day, according to Bryant.

All this makes the experience far different from using conventional AI. When ChatJBT was asked to generate an image, it did not produce one in a matter of seconds. Instead, the website said thousands of people were writing in and that the volunteer group could take days to respond. It offered to send a notification by email or Telegram when a volunteer had replied.

## **Meaningful conversations with ChatTJB**

ChatTJB is receiving far more attention than Bryant expected. One interaction in particular has stayed with him. Someone wrote during their honeymoon, saying they did not feel completely relaxed and asking whether that was normal.

“I think that was the moment the project began to shift from a surreal piece of satire into a place for people to chat in earnest with a well-meaning, if undeniably average, human being,” Bryant told _Fortune_.

While some queries are deeply personal, some are mundane – how to leave a group chat politely, what to eat for dinner, what to wear – and others intriguing – whether hands can have memories of their own.

The draw is not necessarily the expertise. It is the knowledge that someone has actually read the question.

## **What next for ChatTJB?**

Bryant started the service as an art project to generate curiosity among people about their relationship with technology and AI. However, its popularity has got him thinking.

“I really want it to exist long-term, but this isn’t the work that pays me, and running it the way it deserves takes more than one person, so for it to keep going properly, it needs an operating partner or some other form of sponsorship. If that might be you, I’d love to talk.” Bryant was quoted as saying by _CNET_.

# ‘No Muslims in Bharat’ contradicts Hinduism’s essence: Mohan Bhagwat in New York

RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, speaking at a faith leaders’ conference in New York on Saturday, said a Hindu who believes there should be no Muslims in Bharat would not remain true to the essence of Hinduism.

(Photo by Sam PANTHAKY / AFP)](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/08/AFP__20230415__33D83AC__v1__MidRes__IndiaReligionHinduRss-1-2026-08-b81e31da15faa26ef044d992d96a1c1f-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

Chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Mohan Bhagwat speaks during Samajshakti Sangam (Confluence of Social Power) in Ahmedabad on April 14, 2023. (Photo by Sam PANTHAKY / AFP)

[FP News Desk](link_30)|Aug 29, 2026, 23:21:56 IST

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday called for unity and harmony among different faiths while addressing the ‘One World: One Humanity’ faith leaders’ conference in New York.

Speaking alongside several religious leaders, Bhagwat said religions are often defined by rituals, but their larger purpose is to lead people towards truth.

“To follow a religious discipline and pursue the path to divinity, this discipline of rituals is also necessary. But what is the purpose of religion? It leads us to truth,” he said.

Bhagwat said he comes from a society that traditionally believes that religions may be different but humanity remains one.

“I am working in a society that traditionally says that religions might be different, but humanity is one. Truth is one, and humanity is a product of that truth,” he added.

## Bhagwat speaks about India’s traditions

Bhagwat also stressed the need to educate society about India’s ancient traditions and their underlying values.

He said Indian traditions had survived foreign invasions and continued to promote the idea of “one world, one humanity”.

The RSS chief said understanding these traditions was important to appreciating the broader principles of coexistence and harmony.

['If Hindus are awaken...': RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat pushes for unity in diversity in Toronto address](link_31)[Mohan Bhagwat’s unity pitch exposes America’s cancel club](link_32)

## ‘No Muslims’ view not true to Hinduism: Bhagwat

During his address, Bhagwat recalled being asked by members of the Muslim community in 2018 about the RSS’s vision of a Hindu Rashtra.

“If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in Bharat, he is not being true to the essence of Hinduism,” he said.

Bhagwat said Hinduism allows for multiple paths, but these ultimately lead towards the same truth. He also emphasised that there are no fundamental differences between human beings and that everyone is entitled to dignity.

Bhagwat said the RSS had initiated dialogue with Muslim and Christian communities in India, describing dialogue and service as important aspects of its outreach.

“Dialogue is the first step. Service is another but not necessarily a step after dialogue. They have to happen simultaneously. We are serving. And when we serve, we do not discriminate,” he said.

He also acknowledged that the organisation's work often receives less publicity, which he attributed to perceptions shaped by what he called “wrong narratives”.

“That is why, when it comes to publicity, we are far behind. There is a perception created by wrong narratives. But when people actually come and see our work with some understanding, those perceptions can disappear very quickly,” he added.

## Bhagwat comments on modern politics

Bhagwat also spoke about contemporary politics, saying politicians in democratic systems are heavily influenced by public opinion.

He noted that since public opinion plays a major role in democracies, politicians often find it difficult to act against prevailing public sentiment.

# Xi to visit US on Sept 23 for meeting with Trump: Does China hold all trade, geopolitical cards?

Chinese leader Xi Jinping will arrive in the United States for a state visit on September 23, the foreign ministry has confirmed.

Advertisement

![Image 20: US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping while leaving after a visit to the Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing on May 15, 2026. (Photo: Evan Vucci/Pool/Reuters) ](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/Firstpost-1920x1080-50-2026-09-33ef83998ac0c7a9f068fe6bf0bf24f8-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping while leaving after a visit to the Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing on May 15, 2026. (Photo: Evan Vucci/Pool/Reuters) 

[FP News Desk](https://www.firstpost.com/author/fp-staff/)|Sep 21, 2026, 12:59:03 IST

Chinese leader Xi Jinping will arrive in the United States for a state visit on September 23, the foreign ministry has confirmed.

"At the invitation of President of the United States of America Donald J Trump, President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25," the Chinese foreign ministry said in a statement.

Xi will [arrive in Washington DC with all the cards](https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-xi-summit-us-china-policy-american-defeat-expert-14011054.html) as he has won the trade war that Trump launched, forced the United States' retreat from the Indo-Pacific, and chipped away at the American influence in West Asia.

During the state visit, Trump will host a state dinner for Xi, hold bilateral talks, and facilitate interactions of business communities of the two countries. In a rare gesture, Trump is expected to receive Xi at the airport.

## **Xi has cut Trump down to size — and he's complying**

Xi's visit to Washington DC comes months after the two leaders met at the Beijing summit where the power dynamic between the two was clear.

While Trump grovelled and hailed the Chinese leader as “great” and sought a “fantastic future”, [Xi read him the riot act and drew a red line](https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-xi-summit-taiwan-warning-us-china-war-india-japan-message-quad-indo-pacific-14011465.html): the United States would face war if it failed to abide by China’s terms in the Indo-Pacific and elevated Taiwan as the “most important issue” in the US-China relationship.

![Image 21: world](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/earth.svg)More from World

[Why did Trump wear gloves and jacket to welcome Xi Jinping? Is the US prez hiding something?](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/donald-trump-xi-jinping-us-welcome-gloves-jacket-mocking-14047972.html)[B-2 bomber, F-22 Raptors & more: Trump’s red-carpet welcome for Xi Jinping](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/b-2-bomber-f-22-raptors-more-trumps-red-carpet-welcome-for-xi-jinping-14047878.html)

While Trump had been complying with Xi's diktats for a long time, he doubled down after that summit. As soon as the Air Force One took off, he called Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan to tell her to not oppose Chinese plans to invade and occupy Taiwan.

**ALSO READ: [At Beijing summit, Trump and Xi pursued the same goal — making China great again](https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-xi-summit-us-china-relationship-making-china-great-again-taiwan-warning-indo-pacific-14011208.html)**

Last year, Trump acknowledged Xi as an equal and announced the formation of a 'G-2'. In doing so, he did not just elevate China's place in the world order but also accepted America's diminished position. China expert [Prof. Sriparna Pathak told Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/world/donald-trump-xi-jinping-summit-g2-sphere-of-influence-us-china-trade-deal-rare-earths-agreement-trade-war-truce-13947661.html) that Trump played every card he had from tariffs and trade barriers to export controls but eventually decided to shake hands with China “because he realised Xi had won” the battle.

Advertisement

Advertisement

"With G-2's announcement, Trump gave away his conclusion that he had lost to Xi. He also gave away his worldview of carving out spheres of influence with adversaries instead of competing to win. For him, if you cannot bend China, you accept its terms and carve out a consolation prize for yourself," said Pathak.

## **Trump is making China great again**

In his second term, Trump has handed Xi victories on a platter that China had not managed to achieve in decades.

When Trump assumed office, he inherited all the instruments needed to tackle China. Then, step-by-step, [he dismantled all those instruments:](https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-xi-summit-beijing-visit-us-china-relationship-taiwan-indo-pacific-technology-ai-14010960.html) he junked the Quad, which checked Chinese economic and strategic influence; marginalised Aukus, which was meant for military deterrence; unravelled the calibrated export control regime that ensured a technological edge; and undermined collective defence pledges to allies and partners such as the Philippines, Japan, and Taiwan.

China researcher Anushka Saxena told Firstpost that Trump has spent the past 16 months delivering victories to Xi that he has long sought.

Saxena said the Trump’s policy aligns with Chinese interests — not American interests.

"There is no longer a discernible American China strategy. There is only a Trump strategy and it happens to align with China’s preferences. Scolding Tokyo, freezing the Quad, putting Aukus into question, waving through advanced chips to Chinese AI labs — each is something China has lobbied for, and each has now been delivered unilaterally. Trump appears to have granted Xi something he has always wanted: peer‑power status," Saxena told Firstpost.

# BJ Habibie, the Genius of Indonesia's First Aircraft Creator

Translator

[Antara](https://en.tempo.co/reporter/news/1449/antara)

Editor

[Petir Garda Bhwana](https://en.tempo.co/editor/news/991/petir-garda-bhwana)

September 12, 2019 | 06:47 am

[Share Article link copied](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246812/bj-habibie-the-genius-of-indonesias-first-aircraft-creator)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)

![Image 5](https://statik.tempo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871666/871666_720.jpg)

**TEMPO.CO**, **Jakarta** - Indonesia's third president Bacharuddin Jusuf (BJ) Habibie passed away on Wednesday at 6:05 p.m. after being in intensive care at Gatot Subroto Army Hospital in Jakarta since Sunday, September 1. His second-born son Thareq Kemal Habibie said Tuesday that his father was starting to get stable after intensive treatment for exhaustion from his packed activities.

But fate had other plans for [BJ Habibie](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246800/bj-habibie-is-a-role-model-for-the-nation-jokowi). The genius who created Indonesia's first self-made aircraft died at the age 83 Wednesday afternoon, surrounded by his loving family.

BJ Habibie's health had increasingly deteriorated since he underwent surgery in Munich Germany, to treat a leakage in the heart valve prosthesis early March 2018.

But much before the surgery, he never fully recovered mentally or physically from his grief at losing his beloved wife Ainun Habibie in 2010.

He will be buried next to his soulmate Ainun's grave at the Heroes Cemetery, Kalibata, South Jakarta, Thursday.

![Image 6](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871702/871702_720.jpg)

Born in Parepare, South Sulawesi, June 25, 1936, BJ Habibie was the fourth son of eight children of Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie and Tuti Marini Puspowadjojo.

He was a devout Muslim, following his religious family background in Parepare, where his grandfather was an Islamic cleric.

Later in his life, Habibie was one of the founders of the Indonesian Muslim Intellectuals Association (ICMI) and became its patron.

During his adolescence, Habibie went to Christian Dago High School in Bandung, West Java, and then completed his higher education at the Technology Faculty of the University of Indonesia in Bandung (now Bandung Institute of Technology) in 1954.

From 1955 to 1965, Habibie went abroad to study aviation technology majoring in aircraft construction at RWTH Aachen, West Germany.

He graduated and received his Ingenieur diploma in 1960 and became an Ingenieur doctor in 1965 with the highest honors.

Habibie stayed in Germany after his graduation and worked at Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm, an aircraft company in Hamburg.

While he spent most of his adult life overseas, Habibie's love for his motherland never faded.

Even after he received honorary German citizenship for his achievements in aviation technology, he returned home in 1973 when second President Soeharto asked him to work and develop Indonesia with his expertise.

![Image 7](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871701/871701_720.jpg)

Back in Indonesia, his first career was with Pertamina, a state-owned oil and gas company. Then,he was appointed a director at PT Dirgantara Indonesia -- Indonesia's state-owned aviation industry.

Soeharto then appointed Habibie as Minister of Research and Technology in 1978. He occupied that position consecutively until 1997.

During his time as minister, Habibie created the first Indonesian aircraft CN 25 Gatot Kaca that had been manufactured by PT Dirgantara Indonesia.

Habibie was a pioneer in the Indonesian aviation industry as his aircraft had shown the world that Indonesia could move towards an industrial era from being mainly labelled as an agrarian country.

In 1997, his career skyrocketed when the people's assembly (MPR) chose him to be Soeharto's vice president.

Then history turned its page. In 1998, people's power forced Soeharto to step down after nearly 33 years in administration.

On May 21, 1998, Soeharto announced his resignation as president, and legitimately as his vice president, Habibie took over the presidential seat.

The late 1990s was a difficult era, where Indonesia had a severe economic crisis with huge inflation coupled with unstable domestic politics and security.

But [BJ Habibie](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246805/government-declares-three-day-mourning-for-bj-habibie) succeeded in elevating Indonesia from virtual bankruptcy to a relatively safer fundamental economy within only a year and five months of his administration.

![Image 8](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871700/871700_720.jpg)

During his rule, Indonesia had also started regulating the regional autonomy that changed a centralized system into a decentralized one.

Also in his era, a multi-party election was allowed after more than 30 years of Soeharto's regime controlled it to only three parties.

He wrote a long love letter to his late wife as a catharsis for his loss after she died in 2010, and it was published and became one of Indonesia’s best-selling books.

Their love story was also made into at least three movies that still inspire many Indonesians.

Now, the genius aircraft maker has gone, but his legacies will remain forever in the hearts of the children of the nation.

# Turkish top diplomat to visit UAE for Gulf security, Gaza talks

![Image 21: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan (seen) and Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov hold a joint press conference after their meeting in Baku, Azerbaijan, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Turkish Foreign Ministry/Handout)](https://img.turkiyetoday.com/images/2026/9/27/turkish-top-diplomat-to-visit-uae-for-gulf-security-gaza-talks-3229056_20260927132802.jpg)

![Image 22: Photo](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-foto.svg)2

![Image 23: BigPhoto](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-fotobuyut.svg)

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan (seen) and Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov hold a joint press conference after their meeting in Baku, Azerbaijan, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Turkish Foreign Ministry/Handout)

 By **[Newsroom](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/author/newsroom)**

 September 27, 2026 01:45 PM GMT+03:00 

[![Image 24: Newsletters](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/add-preferred-source-g.png) Set as preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=turkiyetoday.com "Add as a preferred source on Google")![Image 25: Share](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-share.svg)

![Image 26: newsletters](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/newsletter.png)

T urkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will visit the United Arab Emirates on Sept. 28 for talks expected to focus on bilateral strategic cooperation, Gulf security, maritime navigation, Yemen, and developments in Gaza and Lebanon, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources.

During the visit, Fidan is expected to review preparations for the second meeting of the Türkiye-UAE High-Level Strategic Council.

He is also expected to reaffirm Türkiye's full solidarity with the UAE, described as one of the countries most adversely affected by the war in the Gulf.

Fidan is expected to argue that outside intervention in the region has contributed to prolonging conflicts and stress the need to strengthen regional ownership in addressing disputes.

![Image 27: Turkish FM Hakan Fidan speaks during an exclusive interview at Turkish House in New York, U.S., September 28, 2024. (AA Photo)](https://img.turkiyetoday.com/images/2026/9/27/turkish-top-diplomat-to-visit-uae-for-gulf-security-gaza-talks-3229056_202609271328_20260927132802_1.jpg)

![Image 28](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-fotobuyut.svg)

 Turkish FM Hakan Fidan speaks during an exclusive interview at Turkish House in New York, U.S., September 28, 2024. (AA Photo) 

## Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Yemen on agenda

Fidan is expected to emphasize the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait for regional and global stability.
He is also expected to say that a unified Yemen that has achieved peace and stability is critical to security in the Middle East.

In Gaza, Fidan is expected to call for moving without delay to the second phase of the Peace Plan, improving humanitarian conditions and beginning reconstruction efforts.

Türkiye and the UAE are among the founding members of the Peace Board, whose work is also expected to be discussed during the visit.

Fidan is also expected to stress the importance of a determined and coordinated international response to preserve and make permanent the ceasefires in Gaza and Lebanon in the face of Israeli attacks.

### Türkiye-UAE trade reached $19.35B in 2025

Türkiye and the UAE have maintained a strategic partnership since 2023.

The first meeting of the High-Level Strategic Council, established the same year, was held at the leaders' level in Ankara on July 16, 2025.

The UAE is the Gulf country with the largest investment presence in Türkiye and Türkiye's biggest trading partner in the Gulf.
Bilateral trade volume reached $19.346 billion in 2025.

Fidan last visited the UAE on March 20, 2026.

# Trump TV launch amid media blackout: What is the White House press pool that has suspended coverage of US president?

The White House has rolled out Trump TV amid his feud with the media. The White House press pool, a dedicated group of journalists that cover the US president, has suspended its coverage after the American leader banned three media outlets, stating they were spreading fake news

Advertisement

![Image 20: US President Donald Trump speaks to the White House press pool in the Oval Office at the White House on September 18. Now, major media outlets have boycotted Trump after CNN, Politico and MS Now were stripped of access by the White House. File image/AFP](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/pool1-2026-09-58ef02e416e1d9b0fa3513ff33cec75d.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

US President Donald Trump speaks to the White House press pool in the Oval Office at the White House on September 18. Now, major media outlets have boycotted Trump after CNN, Politico and MS Now were stripped of access by the White House. File image/AFP

[FP Explainers](https://www.firstpost.com/author/fp-explainers/)|Sep 22, 2026, 09:12:09 IST

On Monday (September 21), the White House launched ‘Trump TV’, a 24-hour streaming platform that will provide viewers with a dedicated platform for presidential content. In an X post, the White House announced, “It’s live. Trump TV is streaming now. 24x7, updated in real time, with top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place. Not every big moment has made it on your TV, now it can.”

The launch of Trump TV comes amid the US president’s fight against several major news organisations over White House press access. This battle has headed for the courts as _CNN_, _MS NOW_ and _Politico_ sued the Trump administration over being barred from the White House, arguing that such a move is in contravention of their First Amendment rights.

This Trump vs media battle has shone a spotlight of the White House press pool and its role in everyday American politics.

Let’s understand what is the White House press pool, why does it matter and what led to this feud?

## What is the White House press pool?

The White House press pool is a designated group of reporters, broadcast journalists and still photographers that cover and travel with the US president, providing news outlets and public with a near-constant stream of information on the American leader’s activities.

![Image 21: explainers](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/explainers.svg)More from Explainers

[‘Quiet, quiet piggy’: Donald Trump insults a woman journalist, and it is not the first time](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/donald-trump-woman-journalist-piggy-us-13951968.html)[‘Press can’t get enough': Why chatty Trump can’t stop answering reporters’ calls](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/us-president-donald-trump-personal-phone-number-reporter-calls-13990495.html)

The White House press pool was created during [President Dwight D Eisenhower](https://www.firstpost.com/world/united-states/presidents-of-the-united-states-dwight-d-eisenhower-the-general-who-took-on-the-nazis-13822235.html)’s term to solve one simple but significant problem – who accompanies the president when he goes on the road or at the White House, as only that many journalists can fit into the Oval Office or Air Force One.

According to Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation, the press pool serves as the eyes and ears of the public inside the White House.

![Image 22](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/pool2-2026-09-9a2943bab4dac8ae9717bde06e0ac95e.jpg)

The White House Press Pool takes cover as Marine One prepares to land at the Ellipse near the White House in Washington, DC. Trump and the media are now in feud with CNN, MS Now and Politico suing the Trump administration for blocking their access to the White House. File image/AFP

The White House press pool covers every media format. Currently, it includes three wire service reporters, two print or online reporters, a radio reporter, four photographers, and a television crew, including a producer, an audio technician and a camera operator. For most of the press pool’s history, the White House Correspondents’ Association controlled which outlets covered the president on any given day

Advertisement

Advertisement

Since its inception, the White House press pool has been present at significant moments in American history. It was there when [John F Kennedy was assassinated](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/history-today-when-john-f-kennedys-assassination-changed-american-politics-13951866.html) in Dallas on November 23, 1963. It was the press pool that gave first-hand accounts of what happened then.

The White House press pool was also present when President[Ronald Reagan was shot](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/history-today-ronald-reagan-assassination-attempt-13874630.html) and was even present when President Donald Trump made the [clandestine plane switch](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/why-trump-secret-plane-switch-has-turned-so-controversial-14037597.html) after the Nato meeting in Turkey in July.

The White House press pool plays a very important role. The journalists in the pool have to cover every aspect of the president’s actions. This means taking detailed notes of everything the US president says or does.

## What led to this feud between Trump and the press pool?

It all began with US President Donald Trump’s Truth Social post on Friday (September 18). The American leader announced that he had [banned _CNN, MS NOW_, and _Politico_ from the White House](https://www.firstpost.com/world/white-house-turns-away-cnn-ms-now-and-politico-journalists-after-trump-announces-ban-14047067.html).

Trump claimed the ban was “a result of their constant ‘reporting’ fake news” and pledged that “other fake news media outlets” would get the same treatment. By Saturday, reporters from those three organisations were being denied White House access.

Akayla Gardner, an _MS Now_ reporter, recounts her experience at the White House on Saturday. “The officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled. I asked why I was not able to get inside. He said it was above him,” she recounted. Reporters from _CNN_ and _Politico_ shared similar experiences.

![Image 23](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/pool4-2026-09-8690910a3806416e74f5bb36ed93d425.jpg)

(From left to right) MS Now White House reporter Akayla Gardner, CNN Senior White House Reporter Betsy Klein and Politico White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett near the White House complex after all were denied entry to the White House and had credentials confiscated following President Donald Trump's ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico. AP

## How have journalists responded to Trump’s ban?

Following these three news organisations facing a Trump ban, other major [television networks extended their solidarity](https://www.firstpost.com/world/us-broadcasters-suspend-white-house-pool-coverage-after-trump-bans-3-outlets-14047387.html), refusing to replace its White House pool crew.

In a rare joint statement, _ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News,_ and _NBC_ said: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No Administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting.”

Others also followed suit. The _Associated Press_ said that it wouldn’t cover the president’s events. “Please be advised that no network travel pool is expected to be with US President Donald Trump today as he heads to New York for the United Nations General Assembly,” read the AP notice.

![Image 24](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/pool5-2026-09-d1b0e7fef414764d9e8bf585a039a246.jpg)

An empty James Brady Press Briefing Room is seen at the White House in Washington. AP

Meanwhile, the _New York Times_ and _Washington Post_ announced they would hold off on publishing or distributing still photographs taken as part of the White House pool coverage on Monday.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Additionally, _CNN, Politico_ and _MS NOW_ have [sued the Trump administration](https://www.firstpost.com/world/cnn-ms-now-and-politico-to-sue-trump-administration-over-white-house-access-ban-14047355.html), arguing that the ban “could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment.”

“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the outlets said in their lawsuit, which is asking the court to act immediately to revive their journalists’ access to the White House.

“And the public at large suffers for however long the unconstitutional ban restricts access to current and complete information about the government.”

The matter is scheduled to be heard in court on Wednesday (September 23). However, for now, a ban remains on the coverage of the US president. The television pool was missing when Trump cut the ribbon to open his new White House helipad. Moreover, administration’s feed was inaudible.

![Image 25](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/09/pool3-2026-09-b92a6c7659465465000e92c7179b10ce.jpg)

Vaughn Hillyard, White House correspondent for MS Now, does a report from near the White House as the media boycotts Trump events. AP

## What does Trump have to say about the feud?

US President Trump has argued that his ban on the three media outlets has nothing to do with free press, but is targeting “fake news”.

“The White House is not instituting an assault on the free press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the fake news, something that has grown like cancer in our beloved United States of America,” Trump said on his social media account on Monday morning. “It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our national security, and must be stopped, now!”

The White House also doubled down, issuing a press release titled “White House access is a privilege — not a right,” in which it argued “the First Amendment protects their right to publish; it does not entitle them to a hard pass, briefing room seat, or place in the press pool”.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration has launched a streaming channel on its site called [Trump TV](https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-tv-goes-live-as-abc-cbs-nbc-fox-cnn-others-halt-shared-white-house-coverage-14047419.html). The stream’s description states, “Watch the Trump Administration’s biggest moments all in one place. Top videos, major remarks, and must-see highlights streaming 24/7 and updated in real time. Stay informed and stay up to date.”

# No fuel, no landing, no tickets: US threatens to ground Iranian airlines globally from Sept 23

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warns foreign aviation firms could lose access to the US dollar system if they continue servicing Iranian airlines

Advertisement

![Image 20: Passengers get off from a privately owned Iranian airline Mahan Air flight at the airport in Kabul on September 15, 2021. (Photo by Karim SAHIB / AFP)](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/07/AFP__20210915__9MV6U6__v2__MidRes__AfghanistanConflict-2026-07-4abc04355930ce0e85f04e5ff49b9ced-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

Passengers get off from a privately owned Iranian airline Mahan Air flight at the airport in Kabul on September 15, 2021. (Photo by Karim SAHIB / AFP)

[FP News Desk](https://www.firstpost.com/author/fp-staff/)|Sep 22, 2026, 12:30:36 IST

All Iranian commercial airlines could effectively be shut out of the global aviation system from September 23, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned, as Washington expands its sanctions campaign against Tehran and targets foreign companies that continue providing services to Iranian carriers.

Bessent said international airports, ground-handling companies and ticketing agents could face US sanctions if they continue to service Iranian airlines. The warning means carriers could struggle to obtain basic services such as fuel, landing assistance and ticket sales outside Iran.

'On September 23rd, all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world,' Bessent told _CNBC_ on Monday. 'If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets, or you will be knocked out of the dollar system.'

The latest move builds on sanctions announced by the US Treasury earlier this month.

On September 8, the Treasury Department sanctioned 36 targets linked to Iran's aviation sector, including 27 Iranian airlines and foreign companies and intermediaries accused of helping Iran procure aircraft, aviation technology and other services.

The Treasury has also warned foreign companies that provide commercial or financial support to sanctioned Iranian airlines that they could themselves face consequences. Simply put, companies that want continued access to the US financial system may have to choose between servicing Iranian carriers and avoiding US sanctions.

![Image 21: world](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/earth.svg)More from World

[China’s $1 trillion trade surplus looms over Trump-Xi summit](https://www.firstpost.com/business/chinas-1-trillion-trade-surplus-looms-over-trump-xi-summit-14047264.html)[Iraq seeks US exemption from Iranian airline sanctions amid travel disruption](https://www.firstpost.com/world/iraq-seeks-us-exemption-from-iranian-airline-sanctions-amid-travel-disruption-14048597.html)

The Treasury has named the wider campaign as Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August to target Iran's financial networks and what Washington calls the regime's economic lifelines. Aviation is one of several sectors targeted under the campaign, alongside shipping, technology, gold and digital assets.

## What happens if airlines continue flying?

The restrictions could make it difficult for Iranian carriers to operate international flights even where the airlines themselves are not formally banned from entering a particular country.

A carrier may technically be allowed to land but still struggle to operate if local companies refuse to provide fuel, ground handling, maintenance, ticketing or other essential services because of the risk of US sanctions.

Advertisement

Advertisement

The threat has already affected Iranian carriers operating abroad.

Mahan Air, one of Iran's biggest private airlines, suspended flights to Turkiye from September 21 after Turkish authorities asked the carrier to stop its services amid concerns over exposure to US sanctions.

## US targets Iran's wider financial network

The aviation measures are part of a broader attempt by the Trump administration to cut Iran off from international finance.

In recent weeks, the Treasury has targeted foreign banks and financial networks accused of helping Tehran evade sanctions. It has also warned financial institutions that facilitating Iranian sanctions evasion could result in exclusion from the US financial system.

The US has previously taken similar action against companies supporting Mahan Air. In July, Treasury sanctioned entities and individuals in countries [including China, India and Russia](https://www.firstpost.com/world/us-sanctions-india-china-and-russia-entities-accused-of-aiding-irans-mahan-air-and-irgc-14035011.html) for providing financial, logistics and commercial support to the airline.

## The China factor

Bessent's latest remarks also come as Washington continues talks with China over Iran and sanctions enforcement.

The Treasury secretary recently held economic discussions with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

China is one of Iran's key economic partners, so Beijing's response to the new US sanctions could be important. Bessent said Chinese financial officials have been in talks with Washington about following the sanctions.

# Mohan Bhagwat’s unity pitch exposes America’s cancel club

Bhagwat pitched for ‘universal oneness’; will the RSS’s critics do the same now?

Advertisement

![Image 20: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addresses the gathering during the Universal Oneness Celebrations, in New York. (PTI)](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/08/Mohan_Bhagwat_1788147489931_1788147490128_18d277b9-6925-41e6-9ff2-5854181550a8-1-2026-08-8f04fe5378299c6dd7c8da3a429f9a20-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addresses the gathering during the Universal Oneness Celebrations, in New York. (PTI)

[Utpal Kumar](https://www.firstpost.com/author/utpal-kumar/)|Aug 31, 2026, 14:23:47 IST

It is rare for both sides of an ideological divide to be unhappy — even outraged — by the same event and, more importantly, by the message emerging from it. Yet, that is precisely what happened after Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed an event at Madison Square Garden in New York on Saturday.

Let’s consider Bhagwat’s words first: “If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same (goal). And every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings.” He went further: “If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu.”

To be fair to Bhagwat, it was a mature articulation of the Indian civilisational perspective, while simultaneously providing an effective rebuttal to those who had opposed the RSS chief’s presence in the United States. More significantly, it offered a striking contrast to the US cancel club, which is liberal in vocabulary but increasingly marked by the instincts of exclusion and cancellation.

Incidentally, a section of the Indian Right is unhappy too, though for the opposite reason. It regards the RSS chief as too conciliatory towards hostile strains of Islamism and Leftism. But that criticism misses the occasion. Bhagwat was speaking at an event devoted to interfaith dialogue. For him to launch into an examination of competing religious doctrines, or the differences between exclusivist Abrahamic traditions and Sanatana traditions, would have defeated the purpose. The event was about multi-faith dialogue. To attend a gathering intended to promote religious harmony and dwell primarily on religious conflict would have been a self-goal.

![Image 21: opinion](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/opinion.svg)More from Opinion

[Flydubai plot reveals the Gulf’s hidden currents that India cannot ignore](https://www.firstpost.com/opinion/flydubai-plot-reveals-the-gulfs-hidden-currents-that-india-cannot-ignore-14050758.html)[Pakistan’s crisis is bigger than Imran Khan](https://www.firstpost.com/opinion/pakistans-crisis-is-bigger-than-imran-khan-14050699.html)

More importantly, Bhagwat articulated the essence of Sanatana Dharma: diversity, dialogue and mutual respect — not merely tolerance. There is an important distinction between respect, accommodation and tolerance. The Sanatana tradition aspires to respect different paths. Modern secularism generally seeks to tolerate them. Exclusivist interpretations of Abrahamic faiths, by contrast, have historically struggled with the proposition that radically different religious paths can possess equal validity.

Bhagwat appeared to have a larger objective: to use an iconic global platform to take Sanatana Dharma’s message of “oneness in different paths” to an international audience. Placed alongside the politics of the American cancel club, the contrast is stark: universal oneness versus selective liberalism; respect for diversity versus cancellation; integration versus confrontation.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Let’s take the case of the current poster boy of American cancel culture, Zohran Mamdani, who had publicly opposed the RSS event in New York, describing its ideology as representing an “exclusionary vision”. Yet, the irony is difficult to miss. A politics that seeks to exclude a speaker because it considers his worldview exclusionary risks reproducing the very instinct it claims to oppose. Moreover, Mamdani, who objected to Bhagwat’s presence, has had no difficulty meeting Imam Siraj Wahhaj, who has publicly expressed opposition to homosexuality and was named as an “unindicted co-conspirator” in connection with the 1993 World Trade Center bombing case. While Mamdani accuses the RSS, and its current leader, Mohan Bhagwat, of “violently” promoting a “supremacist ideology”, he has described Wahhaj as “[one of the nation’s foremost Muslim leaders](https://x.com/ZohranKMamdani/status/1979353018589237717)”.

Herein lies a central contradiction in contemporary ‘liberal’ politics, especially in the West. It advertises pluralism as a cardinal virtue but applies it selectively. Tolerance is readily — and almost exclusively — extended to groups and ideologies regarded as allies; ideological opponents are subjected to demands for exclusion, delegitimisation or cancellation.

Bhagwat’s statement also raises a host of other, harder questions: would similar declarations of theological pluralism be expected from leaders of other religious or ideological organisations? Would Christian or Islamic religious leaders affirm that other religious paths possess equal legitimacy? Would they respect the Bhagavad Gita in the same spirit in which they regard their own sacred texts? Would they affirm that multiple religions can lead to God, truth or salvation?

Not necessarily. And that is precisely where the asymmetry becomes difficult to ignore: the RSS and Bhagwat are frequently treated as uniquely suspect, irrespective of what they actually say, while those on the other side of the religio-ideological divide are treated with kid gloves. This suggests that the issue is not merely the RSS or Bhagwat. It points to a deeper discomfort with Bharat and its civilisational conception of itself.

Bharat often finds itself being cancelled by these very ‘liberals’ and the institutions they control. It is publicly called names, and its civilisational and democratic credentials delegitimised. The annual United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) report is a case in point, routinely attempting to delegitimise the democratic credentials of Bharat, invariably clubbing it with communist China, Islamist Pakistan and autocratic North Korea.

The fact of the matter is that the idea of Bharat is rooted in a civilisation that has, over centuries, absorbed and accommodated extraordinary socio-religious diversity. It offered refuge to persecuted communities, including Parsis and Jews, who were able not merely to preserve their identities but to flourish within the Indic civilisational ecosystem. Jain and Buddhist traditions likewise developed distinctive identities while remaining deeply embedded in the broader Indic world.

Advertisement

Advertisement

These examples complicate simplistic attempts to understand Bharat’s minority issue solely through the Islamic prism. Muslims, of course, constitute a religious minority in the constitutional and demographic sense. But their enormous numbers, internal diversity, long history and profound influence on the subcontinent make the Indian experience very different from the conventional Western image of a tiny minority living precariously alongside an overwhelmingly homogeneous majority. Communities such as Parsis and Jews, Jains and Buddhists offer a more realistic perspective from which to analyse Bharat’s record of civilisational pluralism.

Bharat finds itself in a unique situation where even its supposed allies in the West tend to stand opposed to it, largely because of their innate Christian upbringing, which manifests itself in their outlook despite their outwardly atheistic worldview. Richard Dawkins is a case in point. He fights religious fundamentalism unapologetically. But his lack of understanding of the Sanatana tradition makes him equate it with the Abrahamic faiths he opposes.

A few years ago, Dawkins attacked “Modi’s BJP” as “a tragic affront to India’s secular beginnings”. He described Hinduism as “at least as ridiculous as Islam” and accused contemporary India of betraying the ideals associated with Nehru and Gandhi. Interestingly, he passed this sweeping verdict on “Modi’s India” and “Hinduism” on the basis of an editorial in Nature magazine, which claimed that the Periodic Table and Charles Darwin’s Theory of Evolution had been dropped from the school curriculum in Bharat. As it turned out, it was yet another case of fake news, for the topics had not been removed but merely shifted from Class X to Class XI. The verdict, however, had already been delivered: Hinduism itself was “ridiculous”.

Dawkins is a self-proclaimed atheist, but his cultural assumptions occasionally make him behave like a ‘born-again’ Christian. He criticises PM Modi for foregrounding Hindu identity, yet has described Barack Obama as effectively atheist despite the latter’s very public Christianity. As Micklethwait and Wooldridge observe in _God Is Back_, “one reason why Barack Obama beat Hillary Clinton was that he succeeded in out-Godding her”. Obama himself writes in _The Audacity of Hope_: “Kneeling beneath that cross on the South Side of Chicago, I felt God’s spirit beckoning me. I submitted myself to His will, and dedicated myself to discovering His truth.”

Advertisement

Advertisement

If this is the case with the likes of Dawkins, the general intellectual milieu in the West is largely anti-Bharat. In fact, even someone like Sheldon Pollock, who is projected as a sobering figure in the American Indology arena, especially in comparison with the likes of Wendy Doniger and Audrey Truschke, describes the Ramayana as a “hegemonic discourse” used to legitimise elite domination — specifically by kings and Brahmins — over the masses. He has also argued that the Ramayana’s portrayal of Ravan and the Rakshasas as “others” helped create an ideological template for later hostility towards Muslims.

It is against this larger socio-political and intellectual background that Bhagwat’s Madison Square Garden remarks should be analysed and understood. First, he was participating in an event centred on “Universal Oneness”. His speech naturally reflected that theme. Expecting him to use such an occasion to catalogue religious conflicts would be like looking for culinary advice in an economics textbook.

Second, he was speaking abroad and presenting a civilisational understanding of Bharat and Hinduism to an international audience. Swami Vivekananda’s Chicago address offers a useful historical parallel. Vivekananda spoke differently before Western audiences than he often did in Bharat because his audience, purpose and historical circumstances were different. Third, and most importantly, Bhagwat projected what he regards as the authentic civilisational ethos of Sanatana Dharma: inclusivity without uniformity, unity without erasure and respect for multiple paths without demanding that they become identical.

For decades, Bharat and its traditions have been filtered abroad through a familiar vocabulary: caste, communalism, majoritarianism and religious nationalism. Bhagwat’s intervention attempted to challenge that jaundiced gaze. It placed before an international audience an innately Indian civilisational proposition in which diversity need not be patronisingly tolerated, but genuinely respected and even cherished.

Mohan Bhagwat — first in New York and then in Toronto a day later — pitched “universal oneness”. Will the critics of the RSS do the same now?

# 'If Hindus are awaken...': RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat pushes for unity in diversity in Toronto address

Addressing a gathering at the 'Hindu Vishwa Bandhu - Embrace the World in Friendship' event in Toronto, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat said, 'If Hindus are awake, the world will awaken'

Advertisement

![Image 20: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat. Image: CHORD Canada](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2026/08/ANI-20260831004355-1-2026-08-77ebe5995df63448d855680a0a9ea8e2-1200x675.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat. Image: CHORD Canada

[FP News Desk](https://www.firstpost.com/author/fp-staff/)|Aug 31, 2026, 07:01:32 IST

Addressing a gathering at the "Hindu Vishwa Bandhu - Embrace the World in Friendship" event in Toronto, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat said, "If Hindus are awake, the world will awaken". In his address, Bhagwat emphasised India's intrinsic culture of global helpfulness and unity.

The RSS chief added that India's tradition has always viewed diversity as a natural form of unity. Bhagwat was addressing a high-profile event organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue (CHORD). Reflecting on India's core ethos, [Bhagwat highlighted the universal nature of the Hindu worldview](https://www.firstpost.com/world/no-muslims-in-bharat-contradicts-hinduisms-essence-mohan-bhagwat-in-new-york-14041822.html).

"Whenever Bharat has been asked for help anywhere in the world, it has never refused, and it extends a helping hand even without being asked. This is our tradition, the DNA of Bharat. That is why you may have heard the saying--'If Hindus awaken, the world awakens,'" he said.

Bhagwat noted how Indian spiritual heritage promotes oneness across humanity and nature. "They regard both the animate and the inanimate as their own... They have been taught to see unity in diversity. That is why diversity never poses a problem for unity in India; our tradition teaches us that not only is there unity in diversity, but diversity itself is a form of unity," the RSS Chief added.

## 'True enlightenment lies past external differences': Bhagwat

In his speech, Bhagwat called on the international community to embrace the idea of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam". He emphasised that true enlightenment lies in looking past external differences to recognise the underlying spiritual unity of humanity.

![Image 21: world](https://images.firstpost.com/dlxczavtqcctuei/news18/static/images/fp/revamp_v1/earth.svg)More from World

[Who is Rohan Rane, the Indian on trial in Paris for running neo-Nazi online group that sexually abused girls?](https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/rohan-rane-indian-trial-paris-cvlt-neo-nazi-group-minors-sexually-assaulted-tortured-14050785.html)[Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 awarded to Francis Halzen for detecting cosmic neutrinos](https://www.firstpost.com/world/nobel-prize-in-physics-2026-awarded-to-francis-halzen-for-detecting-cosmic-neutrinos-14050801.html)

"Those who are open-minded and knowledgeable embrace the concept of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam--the belief that the entire earth is one family... While individuals in the material world may differ in body, shape, and complexion, in essence, we are all one. Therefore, serving others is our duty. We have gained this wisdom, which brings us enduring happiness and lasting contentment," he said.

Bhagwat noted that "Bharat" became a [vishwaguru](https://www.firstpost.com/tech/sridhar-vembu-says-india-should-lead-by-sharing-technology-not-hoarding-it-14032563.html) and not a mahashakti. "One may call Bharat a superpower at that time, but it was not a superpower. It served the world. By its own character, it became Vishwaguru, not Mahashakti. So the rise of Bharat means more united, more emancipated humanity," he averred.

Advertisement

Advertisement

"We did it. Long back, when there were no roads, no boats, no aeroplanes, no motor vehicles, only bullock carts and horses-- our ancestors have gone in the regions from Mexico to Siberia, giving them all knowledge. On foot they crossed the Himalayas, went to China, went to Siberia, Mongolia. By small boats they went to Southeast Asia... What did they do? They conquered no country; they converted nobody. Wherever they went, they gave knowledge- astrology, Ayurveda. They imparted the civilizational values," the RSS chief averred.

Bhagwat's address in Toronto came just days after his trip to New York, where he attempted to impart similar values of Hinduism.

# Independence Day amid COVID-19 in the Eyes of Indonesian Diplomats

Translator

[Antara](https://en.tempo.co/reporter/news/1449/antara)

Editor

[Petir Garda Bhwana](https://en.tempo.co/editor/news/991/petir-garda-bhwana)

August 17, 2020 | 12:49 pm

[Share Article link copied](https://en.tempo.co/read/1376646/independence-day-amid-covid-19-in-the-eyes-of-indonesian-diplomats)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)

![Image 5](https://statik.tempo.co/data/2020/08/17/id_960331/960331_720.jpg)

**TEMPO.CO**, **Jakarta** - Indonesian Ambassador to Colombia, Priyo Iswanto, delivered a heartfelt statement as part of his rendition of the 75 th anniversary of Indonesia's [Independence Day](https://en.tempo.co/tag/independence-day) amid the global COVID-19 pandemic.

“All of us, Indonesians here in Colombia, believe that it is not hyperbolic to say that in this pandemic, the situation is rather identical to the time when we were at war. Both the war and the pandemic have led to an irretrievable number of deaths, economic setbacks, and job losses as well as a setback in the fight against poverty,” Iswanto said, as told to ANTARA.

Celebrations of the anniversary of Independence Day, that falls every August 17 for Indonesia, could perhaps be one of the few opportunities for Indonesians residing overseas to bask in a sense of home, including for diplomats and ambassadors, spending time away from home in service to the nation.

Despite only 89 Indonesians residing in Colombia, a smaller number as compared to members of Indonesian diasporas in other nation, all of them would take the once-in-a-year opportunity to come together and echo their nationalism, love, and devotion towards their motherland.

“They would always take the time to participate in activities that would enliven the celebrations at the Embassy grounds, even if the sacred day fell on working days. The day would reflect such a strong sense of unity, as these Indonesians, despite being overseas, would come together, get to know each other, and share their stories,” Iswanto stated while reminiscing about the days when celebrations were held merrily at the Embassy.

However, this year, as Colombian authorities have imposed mandatory quarantine since the end of March until August, it was no longer possible for the Embassy to hold a commemorative event and a gathering for Indonesian nationals.

Iswanto believes that the fervor and enthusiasm to commemorate Independence Day could not be dampened by the pandemic. As a matter of fact, this time of uncertainty can offer a momentum to bolster unity and togetherness.

The absence of crowds will also be apparent during the commemoration of Independence Day at the Indonesian Embassy in Rome, Italy, as Indonesian Ambassador to Italy, Esti Andayani, drew a parallel between the fight against the pandemic and the pre-independence era when war was taking place, albeit the difference lying in the absence of weapons.

“The essence of struggle, however, is the same,” she stated.

Andayani, as a diplomat, called for further measures to be taken to contribute to the true essence of independence today, including through steps to ensure protection of Indonesians overseas.

“During the COVID-19 pandemic, the diplomats tirelessly performed their protection diplomacy duties for Indonesians overseas,” Andayani stated.

In these times of uncertainty amid an unprecedented crisis, protection is one of the most important aspects for those residing outside their own native countries. It also offers a sliver of comfort and hope knowing that despite being in a foreign country away from their kin and not being able to gather with fellow Indonesians to celebrate Independence Day, they are being protected.

However, unlike Rome and Bogota, Indonesians in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, would still be able to bask in the togetherness, as they gather to commemorate the historic beginning of the nation.

Third Secretary of Economy from the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh, A. Yathriba, expressed joy while highlighting the rather conducive situation in the city that allows the Embassy to hold a ceremony in person.

“There were concerns over the possibility of not being able to hold a ceremony, but as it turned out, the situation here is more conducive, which allows us to foster a sense of togetherness with Indonesians here,” she stated.

Yathriba ensured the application of stringent health protocols, including maintaining a safe distance and wearing masks, during this ceremony.

**Intensifying relations**

Apart from working on offering protection and also facilitating the return of Indonesians back home, the diplomats are also conducting their duties to maintain relations with other countries.

“Indonesian diplomats in various countries are also working alongside their partners in the accredited countries in a bid to find treatments and vaccine to end the COVID-19 pandemic,” Ambassador Esti Andayani stated.

Bolstering bilateral relations feature on the list of duties that diplomats are mandated to conduct even amid the pandemic.

Ambassador Iswanto opined that with diplomatic relations between Indonesia and Colombia approaching its 40 th year, the pandemic has, in a way, presented an opportunity to Indonesia to boost its image, as the national carrier flew a route to Colombia for the first time in May, when it facilitated the return of 366 foreign nationals from various nations, including Colombia.

**Keeping the spirit alive**

As handling of the COVID-19 pandemic has gradually became more conducive in Italy, local authorities are still implementing “living with the virus” protocols. With some 14 thousand confirmed cases in mid-August, the Indonesian Embassy in Rome is resorting to virtual celebrations of the Independence Day for Indonesians in Italy, Cyprus, Malta, and San Marino.

From online bazaars with Indonesian foods and products, photo and food plating competitions, to a webinar themed ‘Literacy for the Nation: Writing Creativity and Inspiration,’ the Indonesian Embassy in Rome is making all-out efforts to keep the spirit alive.

In the meantime, the Indonesian Embassy in Bogota is also opting for virtual celebrations through a ceremony and competitions, inviting all Indonesians in Colombia to participate.

“There is a silver lining to holding the ceremony virtually, as 10 Indonesian diasporas in the accredited countries of Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, and St. Christopher and Nevis, can join in the festivities,” Ambassador Priyo Iswanto stated.

While the two Embassies in Bogota and Rome gear up for their virtual events, the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh is preparing its new building for the in-person ceremony since in the start of August, the Embassy had shifted to a new building in front of one of the iconic tourist attractions in the city, the Statue of King Sihanouk.

Akin to those in Bogota and Rome, most people here in Indonesia will also be commemorating the sacred day through the virtual medium, as the central government has prepared several online events to replace those normally held in person.

Despite the distance between one another, be it due to the pandemic or currently being overseas, a sense of oneness would perhaps be felt and exuded a little bit stronger, as the people gather in spirit to be united in the fight against COVID-19, as Indonesia welcomes its 75 th year of [independence day](https://en.tempo.co/tag/independence-day).

# BJ Habibie, the Genius of Indonesia's First Aircraft Creator

Translator

[Antara](https://en.tempo.co/reporter/news/1449/antara)

Editor

[Petir Garda Bhwana](https://en.tempo.co/editor/news/991/petir-garda-bhwana)

September 12, 2019 | 06:47 am

[Share Article link copied](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246812/bj-habibie-the-genius-of-indonesias-first-aircraft-creator)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)[](javascript:void(0);)

![Image 5](https://statik.tempo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871666/871666_720.jpg)

**TEMPO.CO**, **Jakarta** - Indonesia's third president Bacharuddin Jusuf (BJ) Habibie passed away on Wednesday at 6:05 p.m. after being in intensive care at Gatot Subroto Army Hospital in Jakarta since Sunday, September 1. His second-born son Thareq Kemal Habibie said Tuesday that his father was starting to get stable after intensive treatment for exhaustion from his packed activities.

But fate had other plans for [BJ Habibie](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246800/bj-habibie-is-a-role-model-for-the-nation-jokowi). The genius who created Indonesia's first self-made aircraft died at the age 83 Wednesday afternoon, surrounded by his loving family.

BJ Habibie's health had increasingly deteriorated since he underwent surgery in Munich Germany, to treat a leakage in the heart valve prosthesis early March 2018.

But much before the surgery, he never fully recovered mentally or physically from his grief at losing his beloved wife Ainun Habibie in 2010.

He will be buried next to his soulmate Ainun's grave at the Heroes Cemetery, Kalibata, South Jakarta, Thursday.

![Image 6](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871702/871702_720.jpg)

Born in Parepare, South Sulawesi, June 25, 1936, BJ Habibie was the fourth son of eight children of Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie and Tuti Marini Puspowadjojo.

He was a devout Muslim, following his religious family background in Parepare, where his grandfather was an Islamic cleric.

Later in his life, Habibie was one of the founders of the Indonesian Muslim Intellectuals Association (ICMI) and became its patron.

During his adolescence, Habibie went to Christian Dago High School in Bandung, West Java, and then completed his higher education at the Technology Faculty of the University of Indonesia in Bandung (now Bandung Institute of Technology) in 1954.

From 1955 to 1965, Habibie went abroad to study aviation technology majoring in aircraft construction at RWTH Aachen, West Germany.

He graduated and received his Ingenieur diploma in 1960 and became an Ingenieur doctor in 1965 with the highest honors.

Habibie stayed in Germany after his graduation and worked at Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm, an aircraft company in Hamburg.

While he spent most of his adult life overseas, Habibie's love for his motherland never faded.

Even after he received honorary German citizenship for his achievements in aviation technology, he returned home in 1973 when second President Soeharto asked him to work and develop Indonesia with his expertise.

![Image 7](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871701/871701_720.jpg)

Back in Indonesia, his first career was with Pertamina, a state-owned oil and gas company. Then,he was appointed a director at PT Dirgantara Indonesia -- Indonesia's state-owned aviation industry.

Soeharto then appointed Habibie as Minister of Research and Technology in 1978. He occupied that position consecutively until 1997.

During his time as minister, Habibie created the first Indonesian aircraft CN 25 Gatot Kaca that had been manufactured by PT Dirgantara Indonesia.

Habibie was a pioneer in the Indonesian aviation industry as his aircraft had shown the world that Indonesia could move towards an industrial era from being mainly labelled as an agrarian country.

In 1997, his career skyrocketed when the people's assembly (MPR) chose him to be Soeharto's vice president.

Then history turned its page. In 1998, people's power forced Soeharto to step down after nearly 33 years in administration.

On May 21, 1998, Soeharto announced his resignation as president, and legitimately as his vice president, Habibie took over the presidential seat.

The late 1990s was a difficult era, where Indonesia had a severe economic crisis with huge inflation coupled with unstable domestic politics and security.

But [BJ Habibie](https://en.tempo.co/read/1246805/government-declares-three-day-mourning-for-bj-habibie) succeeded in elevating Indonesia from virtual bankruptcy to a relatively safer fundamental economy within only a year and five months of his administration.

![Image 8](https://cdn.tmpo.co/data/2019/09/11/id_871700/871700_720.jpg)

During his rule, Indonesia had also started regulating the regional autonomy that changed a centralized system into a decentralized one.

Also in his era, a multi-party election was allowed after more than 30 years of Soeharto's regime controlled it to only three parties.

He wrote a long love letter to his late wife as a catharsis for his loss after she died in 2010, and it was published and became one of Indonesia’s best-selling books.

Their love story was also made into at least three movies that still inspire many Indonesians.

Now, the genius aircraft maker has gone, but his legacies will remain forever in the hearts of the children of the nation.

# Explainer: Many world leaders died in plane crashes since 1936, while only a few survived

Explainer: Many world leaders died in plane crashes since 1936, while only a few survived

 By **[Ahmet Erarslan](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/author/ahmet-erarslan)**

 May 31, 2024 04:29 PM GMT+03:00 

[![Image 24: Newsletters](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/add-preferred-source-g.png) Set as preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=turkiyetoday.com "Add as a preferred source on Google")![Image 25: Share](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-share.svg)

![Image 26: newsletters](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/newsletter.png)

T he recent helicopter crash involving Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi has drawn attention to other incidents where leaders either survived or perished

Anadolu Agency (AA) compiled a list of helicopter and plane crashes involving heads of state and government dating back to 1936.

On Dec. 9, 1936, then-Swedish Prime Minister Arvid Lindman died when the Douglas DC-2 plane he was in crashed into houses near Croydon Airport in dense fog just after take-off.

On Sept. 7, 1940, Paraguayan President Marshal Jose Felix Estigarribia died in a plane crash.

On July 4, 1943, Polish soldier and statesman Wladyslaw Sikorski, who led Poland's government in exile during World War II, died when his plane crashed in Gibraltar.

On June 16, 1958, the then Interim President of Brazil, Nereu Ramos, died when a plane belonging to Cruzeiro Airlines crashed.

On March 29, 1959, Barthelemy Boganda, president of the Central African Republic and a hero of independence, passed away after his plane crashed.
On Sept. 18, 1961, the plane of then-U.N. Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjold, who was on duty to mediate peace in the Congo, crashed in today's Zambia. Some 16 people, including Hammarskjold, died in the accident.

On April 13, 1966, Iraqi President Abdul Salam Arif died in a helicopter crash. Arif came to power through a coup in February 1963.

On April 27, 1969, Bolivian President Rene Barrientos died when his helicopter crashed in the city of Cochabamba.

On Jan. 18, 1977, Yugoslavian Prime Minister Dzemal Bijedic's Learjet 25 plane crashed into Inac Mountain near the city of Kresevo in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Bijedic, his wife and six other people died in the accident.

On May 27, 1979, a plane carrying Mauritanian Prime Minister Ahmed Ould Bouceif, who was going to attend an African summit, crashed off the coast of Dakar. Bouceif died in the accident.

On Dec. 4, 1980, Portuguese Prime Minister Francisco Sa Carneiro and Defense Minister Adelino Amaro da Costa died when their plane crashed in the capital Lisbon just after takeoff.
On May 24, 1981, Ecuadorian President Jaime Roldos Aguilera and Defense Minister Maj. Gen. Marco Subia Martinez lost their lives when the plane they were on crashed near the Peruvian border.

On July 31, 1981, Panamanian President Omar Torrijos died when the small plane he was flying crashed into a forest.

On Oct. 19, 1986, a twin-engine plane carrying Mozambican President Samora Machel and several Mozambican ministers crashed near the Mozambique-South African border. Thirty-three people died in the accident including Machel, some ministers and high-ranking officials of the Mozambican government.

In the investigations carried out after the accident, the pilot was found guilty.

On June 1, 1987, Lebanese Prime Minister Rashid Karami lost his life when a bomb exploded in the helicopter he was on board to go to Beirut. The remote-controlled bomb, weighing approximately 300 grams and placed behind the seat where he would sit, was detonated shortly after it took off. Only Karami died in the accident.
On Aug. 17, 1988, a C-130 military aircraft carrying Pakistani President Zia-ul-Haq, his five generals and U.S. Ambassador Arnold Lewis Raphel crashed near Bahawalpur, approximately 530 kilometers (329.3 miles) south of the capital Islamabad. In the accident in which there were no survivors, investigators focused on the possibility of sabotage.

On April 6, 1994, a plane carrying Burundi's President Cyprien Ntaryamira and Rwandan President Juvenal Habyarimana was fired on near Kigali Airport. There were no survivors from the plane that crashed in the area where the presidential palace is located.

On February 26, 2004, a plane carrying Boris Trajkovski, who served as the second president of Macedonia, and his accompanying delegation crashed near the city of Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Eight people, including Trajkovski and his advisors, died in the accident.

An international commission established to investigate the plane crash announced in a report shared with the public after two years of research that the plane crash was the result of "pilot error.”
On April 10, 2010, a Tupolev 154 plane carrying 96 people including Poland's President Lech Kaczynski and his wife arrived at Russia's Smolensk Airport, where they were to attend a ceremony commemorating the Katyn Massacre, in which approximately 22,000 Poles were executed during the Stalin period. While landing, the plane crashed into a forest area. There were no survivors.

On February 5, 2024, a Robinson R-66 helicopter carrying former Chilean President Sebastian Pinera and his entourage crashed into Lake Ranco in the Los Rios region.

The helicopter crashed shortly after takeoff because of heavy rain and dense fog. Three people managed to jump into the lake and get to shore Pinera died because he could not unfasten his seat belt.

## Heads of state who survived plane or helicopter crashes

On Apr. 11, 1955, Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai survived an assassination attempt on an Air India plane he had chartered for Indonesia. Zhou, who changed his travel plans at the last minute upon notice, did not board the plane.
The plane crashed into the South China Sea after a bomb exploded. Eleven passengers lost their lives and three survived.

On Feb. 17, 1959, Adnan Menderes, the ninth prime minister of Türkiye, was 4.5 kilometers away from Gatwick Airport in London, where he had gone to sign an agreement on Cyprus between Türkiye, England and Greece.

He survived when his plane crashed. In the accident, 14 people, including then Anadolu Director-General Serif Arzik, lost their lives and seven people, including the crew and passengers, were injured.

On Feb. 9, 1977, former Queen of Jordan A Alia Toukan died in a helicopter crash in the city of Tafila. Toukan's husband, King Hussein bin Talal, survived the accident. The Jordanian Minister of Health at the time, Mohammed al‐Beshir, lost his life in the accident, which occurred because of a violent rainstorm.

In June 1994, King Charles III of England, who was the Prince of Wales at the time, lost control of the plane he was flying because of strong winds, causing it to crash. Although no one was injured in the incident, more than $1 million of damage occurred.

# 10 world leaders who died in air crashes

Air crashes involving world leaders often spark intense scrutiny and speculation as the circumstances surrounding these incidents are subjected to rigorous investigation and analysis

Reuters](https://images.firstpost.com/uploads/2024/05/PolishPlaneCrashMemorial1200Reu-2024-05-d1bcf68f18fd23d9c0292eafad6bab77.jpg?im=Resize,width=720,aspect=fit,type=normal)

[FP Staff](https://www.firstpost.com/author/fp-staff/)|May 21, 2024, 19:40:52 IST

The deaths of world leaders in air crashes are pivotal moments in history shaking up politics and leaving nations in uncertainty. These incidents not only rob countries of influential figures but also create power vacuums and prompt questions about the future. As investigations unfold speculation runs rampant and the events often become shrouded in conspiracy theories. Here is a list of 10 world leaders who died in air crashes:

**1. Ebrahim Raisi (1960-2024):** President Raisi and Foreign Minister Amirabdollahian (1964-2024) along with others who were on board the helicopter that crashed are dead, multiple Iranian news agencies confirmed.

**2. General Zia-ul-Haq (1924-1988):** The sixth president of Pakistan died in a plane crash near Bahawalpur, Pakistan. The cause of the crash remains controversial with speculation about mechanical failure, sabotage and conspiracy theories.

**3. Lech Kaczynski (1949-2010):** The president of Poland died in a plane crash near Smolensk, Russia along with many other high-ranking Polish officials. The crash occurred as the delegation was en route to commemorate the Katyn massacre.

**4. Ramon Magsaysay (1907-1957):** The seventh president of the Philippines died in a plane crash on Mount Manunggal in Cebu. Magsaysay was known for his strong anti-communist policies and his dedication to democracy.

**5. Juvenal Habyarimana (1937-1994):** The president of Rwanda and Cyprien Ntaryamira (1955-1994), the president of Burundi, both died when their plane was shot down as it was about to land in Kigali, Rwanda. This incident is often cited as the trigger for the Rwandan genocide.
